summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates how a man who made governors laugh was warned, with Bilaal bin Haarith's hadith on the weight of a single word.
notes: Alqama's grandfather (who gives the warning) is unnamed and not tagged; Muzani may be the same person. The second paragraph is a variant chain. Alqama bin Waqqaas is not clearly the approved 'alqama' entry, so tagged as null.

summary: Hudhayfa warns against the doors of rulers, where a person confirms their lies and praises them falsely.
notes: The questioner is unnamed. Text ends with stray OCR debris.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates his father Abbaas's three pieces of advice on serving the ruler: fear Allaah, never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite in his presence.
notes: 'Ameerul Mu'mineen' is not named in this text (Umar from context), so not tagged. Aamir is a narrator in the chain who speaks; sahabi status not stated.

summary: Sha'bi reports Abbaas's advice to his son Abdullaah about Umar: never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite about anyone in his presence.
notes: A variant of n00843 with the same advice, here naming Umar. Sha'bi is not in the approved list.

summary: Hasan narrates that Umar refused a verse from Ubay bin Ka'b, and when Ubay said he had heard it from the Prophet, Umar admitted the truth and said there is no good in a ruler in whose presence the truth cannot be spoken.
notes: Tagged as the approved 'hasan' entry because the text gives RA; check that this is the intended Hasan.

summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that Umar accused Ubay of lying about a verse, Ubay answered that Umar's lie was worse, and then Umar confirmed Ubay had spoken the truth.
notes: The person who reprimanded Ubay is unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that when Umar asked a gathering what they would do if he became permissive, Basheer bin Sa'd promised to set him straight like an arrow.
notes: Umar's closing words are garbled by OCR, so his exact reply is uncertain.

summary: Moosa bin Abu Isa reports that Muhammad bin Maslama told Umar that if he strayed they would straighten him, and Umar praised Allaah for placing him among such people.
notes: A footnote reference (Ibn Raahway, Kanzul Ummaal) is ignored.

summary: Abu Qabeel reports that Mu'aawiya declared from the pulpit that the wealth was theirs to give or withhold, and a man objected three Jumu'ahs running; Mu'aawiya then recalled the Prophet's warning about rulers who speak wrongly and were thankful to the man for waking him.
notes: The text says only 'Hadhrat Mu'aawiya'; identified as Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan from context, not confirmed. The objecting man is unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed rebuked Abu Ubaydah for harshly punishing non-Muslims over the jizya, citing the Prophet's warning about the severest punishment on the Day of Qiyaamah.
notes: The text says 'Kuffaar' for the people punished.

summary: Hasan reports that when Ziyaad appointed Hakam bin Amr governor of Khurasan, Hakam refused Mu'aawiya's order to withhold the gold and silver and distributed the booty, and Mu'aawiya had him arrested so he died in shackles.
notes: Ziyaad is named by first name only and is not in the approved list (probably Ziyaad bin Abihi, unconfirmed). Hakam's death is given in two versions, both included. Mu'aawiya is identified from context. Hasan tagged as the approved 'hasan' entry.

summary: Ataa reports that Imraan bin Husayn, sent to collect zakaah, distributed it to the needy instead of bringing it back, and Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit reports Umar's custom of appointing governors before witnesses and holding them to account.
notes: Two reports are joined. A passage between them is missing, so the transition is unclear. 'Ziyaad or his son' is ambiguous in the text, so Ziyaad is tagged as a null name.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Umar appointed Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi to lead a regiment for jihaad, telling him it was not to whip or humiliate them but to fight and share the booty.
notes: Ends with stray footnote debris '(,3)'. Sa'eed's reply is garbled by OCR.

summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari tells the people that Umar sent him to teach them the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Nabi and to administer municipal affairs.
notes: A short speech with no chain of narration.

summary: Abu Saalih Ghifaari reports that Amr bin Al Aas offered Umar a house in Egypt, and Umar refused and turned the plot into a marketplace for the Muslims.
Tameem Jayshani reports that Umar wrote to Amr bin Al Aas ordering him to demolish a pulpit from which he rose above the people's necks.
notes: OCR reads 'M Aas' which is taken as Amr bin Al Aas. Tameem Jayshani is not in the approved list.

summary: Abu Uthmaan reports that Umar wrote to Utba bin Farqad that his position and wealth were not his own efforts, telling him to feed the people as he feeds himself and avoid luxury, silk and imitating the mushrikeen.
notes: The opening 'wrote a letter to them' is unclear. The text does not state Utba's sahabi status.

summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Umar had the lofty residence of the governor of Hims burned and made him fetch water for the camels, then told him that his short time in this world did not justify such a building.
notes: 'During the Hay' is OCR for Hajj. The governor of Hims and the messenger are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Attaab bin Rifaa'ah reports that Umar sent Muhammad bin Maslama to bring Sa'd to account for his mansion, and Abu Moosa reports that Abu Ubaydah, having been ordered to move his people away from a plague, died of it himself.
notes: Two stories are joined: Sa'd's mansion, and Abu Ubaydah's plague death. The join is garbled and part of a letter is missing. The text gives only 'Sa'd'; tagged as Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas from context. Abu Moosa is both narrator and participant in the plague account.

summary: Abu Ubaydah replies to Umar's letter that he will not leave the army to save his own life, and asks to be released from his command so he can stay with his soldiers.
notes: Continues n00859. The heading names Sa'd, but the content is Abu Ubaydah's reply. The narrator is not named.

summary: Abu Ja'far reports that the Prophet asked Abu Usayd whether he had sold a weeping captive woman's son, and Muhammad bin Sallaam reports that Umar removed an official who had lost his mercy, saying those without mercy for their own children cannot show it to the masses.
notes: Two narrations are joined. The removed official is unnamed. A footnote citation (Ibn Asaakir, Kanzul Ummaal) is ignored.

summary: Urwa reports that when the Makhzoomiyyah woman's penalty for theft was to be waived through Usaama, the Prophet refused and had her hand cut off, saying even Faatima would be punished if she stole, and afterwards she repented and married.
notes: The text says 'Hadhrat Urwa (RA)' only. urwa-bin-zubayr is chosen from the context of this well-known report (Aa'isha is the one speaking at the end); not confirmed by the text. The woman is unnamed.

summary: Abu Qataadah relates that after Hunayn he killed a mushrik and claimed the dead man's possessions, the Prophet confirmed his right to them, and he bought an orchard with them, his first wealth as a Muslim.
notes: Not the approved 'qataada' entry (a different person). The man who spoke for the claimant is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad reports that he sold his shawl and turban to a Jew to pay a four-dirham debt when the Prophet ordered him to pay, and an old woman gave him a shawl.
notes: The Jewish creditor and the old woman are unnamed. Text gives 'Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad Aslami (RA)' as narrator and subject.

summary: Ummu Salama reports that the Prophet refused to judge in favour of the stronger claimant in an inheritance dispute between two Ansaar men, warning that it would be a yoke of Jahannam, and told them to divide the right and draw lots.
notes: The two Ansaar men are unnamed. Ummu Salama is tagged as the approved 'umm-salama' entry, not 'umm-salma'.

summary: Abu Sa'eed reports that a Bedouin harshly demanded a debt from the Prophet, and the Prophet borrowed dates from Khowia bint Qais to repay him with extra, saying a nation whose weak cannot claim their rights without hesitation has no good in it.
notes: The Bedouin and the companions are unnamed. Khowia bint Qais has no approved entry; may be the same person as Khowla bint Qais in n00867 (not confirmed).

summary: Khowla bint Qais reports that the Prophet owed dates to a man from Banu Saa'idah, and when an Ansaari paid him inferior dates he refused, and the Prophet wept, said the nation whose weak cannot claim their rights is not blessed, and ordered the debt settled.
notes: The text says Khowla was the wife of Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib. This is not confirmed by other sources and may be an error, so Hamza is only tagged as mentioned. Whether Khowla and Khowia (n00866) are the same person is unclear. The Banu Saa'idah man and the Ansaari are unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr struck a man who entered the Zakaah camels without permission, then gave him the rein to take revenge, and when Umar intervened Abu Bakr compensated him with a camel, a carriage, a blanket and five dinaars.
notes: The man and the woman who sent the rein are unnamed.

summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar and Ubay bin Ka'b took a dispute to Zaid bin Thaabit, who seated Umar at the head of the bedding, which Umar rejected, and Umar then took the oath as a common Muslim would; the Ibn Asaakir version gives a date-harvest dispute.
notes: Ibn Asaakir is cited as a reference, not tagged. Sha'bi is the same narrator as n00844.

summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar asked Abbaas to sell or give his house by the Prophet's Masjid for the expansion, and when Abbaas refused, Ubay bin Ka'b ruled that no one may be removed from his house without consent, citing the Prophet's account of Sulaymaan.
notes: Continues in n00871. Ubay's citation (Bayhaqi, Kanzul Ummaal) is ignored. Sulaymaan is a prophet, not a Companion.

summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Ubay bin Ka'b decided in Abbaas's favour, telling the story of Sulaymaan buying land at a price he had to accept, and Abbaas then gave the house as sadaqah for the Muslims.
notes: The embedded story of Sulaymaan buying land is quoted from Ubay. The seller is unnamed. 'Abdur Razzaaq' citation is ignored.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah drank wine in Egypt, were punished by Amr bin Al Aas at his own request, and Umar later punished Abdur Rahmaan further, who died a month later from an unrelated cause.

people.name: Abdur Rahmaan bin Umar bin Khattaab

notes: Abdullaah is both narrator and participant in the story. 'Abu Saroo'ah' spelling as in the text.

summary: Hasan narrates that Umar sent for a woman whose husband had gone missing, and she was so frightened that she went into labour; Umar then rebuked the one responsible for the killing.
notes: Badly garbled by OCR with footnote text mixed in (Abdur Razzaaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Asaakir, Saalim Abu Nadhar, Bayhaqi are references and not tagged). A middle section is missing, and the text is cut off mid-sentence. Variant mentions Hudhayfa instead of Ubay. The woman and the man are unnamed. Hasan is tagged as the approved 'hasan' entry.

summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Umar was grieved when a governor's men drowned an old man who was forced into a cold river, and Umar ordered the governor to pay the blood money and leave, saying one Muslim was worth more than all his conquests.
notes: The governor (called 'the Ameer' in the text) and the old man are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Jareer reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari gave a man twenty lashes and shaved his head over a dispute about his share of booty, and Umar ordered that the revenge be taken in the same way, but the man forgave him for the pleasure of Allaah.
notes: The text is cut off after the forgiveness line ('W'). The man is unnamed. 'Jareer' has no RA in the text, so the approved 'jareer' (unsure) entry is used.

summary: Hirmaazi reports that Umar summoned Fayrooz Daylami, who slapped a Qurayshi youth in a dispute over entry, and when Umar cited the Prophet's words about Fayrooz killing the false prophet Aswad Anasi, the youth forgave him and Fayrooz gave him his sword, horse and thirty thousand.
notes: The Qurayshi youth is unnamed. Hirmaazi is not in the approved list, and is not the same as the 'hirmaas-bin-ziyaad' entry.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that a slave woman whose master burned her private parts on a false accusation of fornication was freed by Umar, who lashed the master a hundred times and cited the Prophet's ruling that no retribution is taken from a master for his slave, and that anyone burned is freed.
notes: The slave woman and her master are unnamed.

summary: Makhool reports that Ubaadah bin Saamit struck a non-Arab Christian labourer who refused to hold his animal, and Umar ruled that Ubaadah should pay compensation instead of allowing retaliation, after Zaid bin Thaabit objected to retaliation against Umar's brother.
notes: The labourer is unnamed. Makhool is not in the approved list. Makhool's sahabi status is set to 'no' as he is generally a follower (tabi'i).

summary: Suwayd bin Ghafala reports that Umar, on hearing a dhimmi had been beaten by a Muslim, had Awf bin Maalik punished after learning that Awf had struck a man who raped a Muslim woman, and crucified the rapist, saying there would be no protection for such a dhimmi.
notes: The complainant and the rapist are unnamed. The text uses both 'Ahlul Kitaab' and 'the Jew'. Footnote citation (Bayhaqi, Kanzul Ummaal) ignored. The woman's relatives are unnamed.

summary: Abdul Malik bin Ya'la reports that Bakr bin Shaddaah confessed to killing a Jew who had insulted a Muslim's wife, and Umar acquitted him because of the Prophet's prayer that his speech be truthful.
notes: The Jew and the Muslim husband are unnamed; the husband is called 'Ash'ath' in the Jew's words, not tagged. Part of the Prophet's prayer line is garbled by OCR.
